newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE SET TO ANNOUNCE FLOTATION PLANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE SET TO ANNOUNCE FLOTATION PLANS.

text.p: English premier league club Newcastle United, who have just installed Kenny Dalglish as their manager, were preparing on Wednesday to reveal details of their planned stock market flotation.
Club press officer Graham Courtney said Newcastle would issue a statement on Thursday on a flotation which experts say will value the club at some 160 million pounds ($265 million).

Details of the flotation timetable and offer structure are awaited following Newcastle's announcement last month that it planned a listing to finance the next phase of its growth. Trading in the shares is likely to begin by April.

There has also been speculation that Newcastle chairman Sir John Hall, a property magnate who has pumped millions of pounds into the club, will take on the lower profile role of life president, perhaps handing over the day-to-day running of the club to his son Douglas.
The flotation looked in danger of being blown off course last week by the storm created by Kevin Keegan's shock decision to quit as manager after five years in charge.

But calm has been restored thanks to the appointment of former Liverpool and Blackburn Rovers manager Dalglish on Tuesday night. The arrival of Dalglish was welcomed by financial players as well as Newcastle fans.

"Management is obviously an important issue for the City (financial institutions) and if you can't have continuity then a man with a proven track record like Dalglish is the next best thing," said Nick Knight, who has researched soccer club finances for brokerage Nomura.
"The people of Newcastle may not think so but this may turn out to be a blessing in disguise."
Dalglish has already tasted title success as a manager with Liverpool and Blackburn. No manager has ever won the English championship with three different clubs.

Dalglish's Newcastle team is expected to be less spectacular than the one Keegan built but the hope is that he will rectify the glaring defensive weaknesses which undermined the goalscoring feats of England duo Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand.
Newcastle are still in contention for the league title and the F.A. and UEFA Cups this season.
They are the latest in a long line of British soccer clubs seeking to raise new funds and broaden ownership by joining the stock market.

The game is booming, with satellite broadcaster BSkyB pumping huge sums of money into the English premier league and fans flocking through the turnstiles at modernised stadiums as hooliganism declines.

English champions Manchester United are the model which clubs are seeking to emulate in the financial stakes. United's success on the pitch has been matched by big profits off it and the club is now valued at over 400 million pounds.

Smaller premier league clubs such as Sunderland and Southampton, for whom survival in the top flight is the name of the game, have also seen their shares climb steeply in value since they joined the stock market recently.

Dealers believe there will be strong interest in the Newcastle listing. "They will be the second-biggest quoted club in the market after Manchester United and I think they will do very well," said Alon Bull of Winterflood Securities. ($1=.5979 Pound)
